([GitHub](https://github.com/openstack/kolla-ansible)) - *Use when* you're deploying OpenStack and want containerized services via Ansible. *Avoid when* you're not running OpenStack.
summary: Ansible playbooks for deploying OpenStack.
use_when: You're deploying OpenStack and want containerized services via Ansible.

avoid_when: You're on the latest Ansible versions where compatibility may lag.
name: Mitogen for Ansible
raw: - [Mitogen for Ansible](https://mitogen.networkgenomics.com/ansible_detailed.html) OSS - Ansible accelerator to speed up module execution and reduce SSH overhead. ([GitHub](https://github.com/mitogen-hq/mitogen)) - *Use when* Ansible playbook execution is slow due to SSH overhead on many hosts. *Avoid when* you're on the latest Ansible versions where compatibility may lag.
summary: Ansible accelerator to speed up module execution and reduce SSH overhead.
use_when: Ansible playbook execution is slow due to SSH overhead on many hosts.

avoid_when: You want agentless simplicity or your team doesn't want to learn Puppet DSL.
name: Puppet
raw: - [Puppet](https://puppet.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Configuration management and automation; open source core with enterprise features. ([GitHub](https://github.com/puppetlabs/puppet)) - *Use when* you need a mature, agent-based system with strong state enforcement and reporting. *Avoid when* you want agentless simplicity or your team doesn't want to learn Puppet DSL.
summary: Configuration management and automation; open source core with enterprise features.
use_when: You need a mature, agent-based system with strong state enforcement and reporting.

avoid_when: Community Ansible and AWX cover your needs.
name: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform
raw:
- [Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/management/ansible) - Enterprise automation platform built around Ansible.
    - *Use when* you need enterprise support, RBAC, and a centralized dashboard for Ansible at scale. *Avoid when* community Ansible and AWX cover your needs.
summary: Enterprise automation platform built around Ansible.
use_when: You need enterprise support, RBAC, and a centralized dashboard for Ansible at scale.

avoid_when: Your team prefers code-first workflows over GUI-driven management.
name: Rudder
raw: - [Rudder](https://www.rudder.io/) Open-core / SaaS - Continuous configuration and automation platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/Normation/rudder)) - *Use when* you want continuous compliance with a web UI and audit trails out of the box. *Avoid when* your team prefers code-first workflows over GUI-driven management.
summary: Continuous configuration and automation platform.
use_when: You want continuous compliance with a web UI and audit trails out of the box.

avoid_when: The learning curve for states/pillars/grains feels excessive for your team size.
name: Salt
raw: - [Salt](https://saltproject.io/) OSS - Event-driven automation and configuration management. ([GitHub](https://github.com/saltstack/salt)) - *Use when* you need event-driven, highly scalable remote execution and config management. *Avoid when* the learning curve for states/pillars/grains feels excessive for your team size.
summary: Event-driven automation and configuration management.
use_when: You need event-driven, highly scalable remote execution and config management.

avoid_when: Workloads are long-running, latency-sensitive (cold starts), or you want cloud portability.
name: AWS Lambda
raw:
- [AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/) - Serverless compute service by AWS.
    - *Use when* you need event-driven, short-lived functions tightly integrated with AWS services. *Avoid when* workloads are long-running, latency-sensitive (cold starts), or you want cloud portability.
summary: Serverless compute service by AWS.
use_when: You need event-driven, short-lived functions tightly integrated with AWS services.

avoid_when: You need full Kubernetes control or are not on Azure.
name: Azure Container Apps
raw:
- [Azure Container Apps](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/container-apps/) - Azure service for running containerized apps.
    - *Use when* you want serverless containers on Azure with built-in scaling and Dapr integration. *Avoid when* you need full Kubernetes control or are not on Azure.
summary: Azure service for running containerized apps.
use_when: You want serverless containers on Azure with built-in scaling and Dapr integration.

avoid_when: Your functions exceed execution time limits or you want cloud-agnostic FaaS.
name: Azure Functions
raw:
- [Azure Functions](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/functions/) - Managed serverless compute service by Azure (runtime host is open source). ([GitHub](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-host))
    - *Use when* you need event-driven compute tightly integrated with Azure services. *Avoid when* your functions exceed execution time limits or you want cloud-agnostic FaaS.
summary: Managed serverless compute service by Azure (runtime host is open source).
use_when: You need event-driven compute tightly integrated with Azure services.

avoid_when: You're fine using the managed Azure Functions service directly.
name: Azure Functions Host
raw: - [Azure Functions Host](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-host) OSS - The runtime host and core execution engine for Azure Functions. - *Use when* you want to self-host or debug the Azure Functions runtime locally. *Avoid when* you're fine using the managed Azure Functions service directly.
summary: The runtime host and core execution engine for Azure Functions.
use_when: You want to self-host or debug the Azure Functions runtime locally.

avoid_when: You need container-level flexibility or are not on GCP.
name: Google Cloud Functions
raw:
- [Google Cloud Functions](https://cloud.google.com/functions) - Event-driven serverless functions on Google Cloud.
    - *Use when* you need lightweight functions integrated with GCP services and Firebase. *Avoid when* you need container-level flexibility or are not on GCP.
summary: Event-driven serverless functions on Google Cloud.
use_when: You need lightweight functions integrated with GCP services and Firebase.

avoid_when: You need persistent connections, GPU workloads, or non-HTTP triggers natively.
name: Google Cloud Run
raw:
- [Google Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run) - Serverless containers on Google Cloud.
    - *Use when* you want serverless containers with any language/framework and pay-per-request pricing. *Avoid when* you need persistent connections, GPU workloads, or non-HTTP triggers natively.
summary: Serverless containers on Google Cloud.
use_when: You want serverless containers with any language/framework and pay-per-request pricing.

avoid_when: You don't already operate Kubernetes or want fully managed FaaS.
name: Knative
raw: - [Knative](https://knative.dev/) OSS - Kubernetes-based platform to deploy and manage serverless workloads. ([GitHub](https://github.com/knative)) - *Use when* you want vendor-neutral serverless on your own Kubernetes clusters. *Avoid when* you don't already operate Kubernetes or want fully managed FaaS.
summary: Kubernetes-based platform to deploy and manage serverless workloads.
use_when: You want vendor-neutral serverless on your own Kubernetes clusters.

avoid_when: You need enterprise scale without paying for the Pro tier.
name: OpenFaaS
raw: - [OpenFaaS](https://www.openfaas.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Functions-as-a-Service framework for Kubernetes; OSS core with commercial Pro features. ([GitHub](https://github.com/openfaas/faas)) - *Use when* you want a simple, portable FaaS layer on Kubernetes or Docker Swarm. *Avoid when* you need enterprise scale without paying for the Pro tier.
summary: Functions-as-a-Service framework for Kubernetes; OSS core with commercial Pro features.
use_when: You want a simple, portable FaaS layer on Kubernetes or Docker Swarm.

avoid_when: Your language/runtime doesn't compile to Wasm or you need broad ecosystem maturity.
name: Spin
raw: - [Spin](https://spinframework.dev/) OSS - Framework for building and running serverless WebAssembly applications. ([GitHub](https://github.com/spinframework/spin)) - *Use when* you want ultra-fast cold starts and sandboxed Wasm-based serverless. *Avoid when* your language/runtime doesn't compile to Wasm or you need broad ecosystem maturity.
summary: Framework for building and running serverless WebAssembly applications.
use_when: You want ultra-fast cold starts and sandboxed Wasm-based serverless.

avoid_when: You need advanced RBAC, drift detection, or a managed solution.
name: Atlantis
raw: - [Atlantis](https://www.runatlantis.io/) OSS - Terraform pull-request automation. ([GitHub](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis)) - *Use when* you want self-hosted, GitOps-style `plan`/`apply` in pull requests. *Avoid when* you need advanced RBAC, drift detection, or a managed solution.
summary: Terraform pull-request automation.
use_when: You want self-hosted, GitOps-style `plan`/`apply` in pull requests.

avoid_when: You want a fully self-hosted or open-source solution.
name: Env0
raw:
- [Env0](https://www.env0.com/) - Infrastructure as Code automation and governance platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/env0))
    - *Use when* you need managed IaC workflows with cost governance and environment-as-a-service. *Avoid when* you want a fully self-hosted or open-source solution.
summary: Infrastructure as Code automation and governance platform.
use_when: You need managed IaC workflows with cost governance and environment-as-a-service.

avoid_when: You need an all-in-one platform with state management and a dashboard.
name: OpenTaco
raw: - [OpenTaco](https://opentaco.dev/) OSS - Terraform/OpenTofu CI orchestration and pull-request automation. ([GitHub](https://github.com/diggerhq/digger)) - *Use when* you want open-source PR automation that runs in your own CI (no separate server). *Avoid when* you need an all-in-one platform with state management and a dashboard.
summary: Terraform/OpenTofu CI orchestration and pull-request automation.
use_when: You want open-source PR automation that runs in your own CI (no separate server).

avoid_when: Atlantis or native CI pipelines suffice.
name: Scalr
raw:
- [Scalr](https://www.scalr.com/) - Terraform automation and collaboration software. ([GitHub](https://github.com/Scalr))
    - *Use when* you need a Terraform Cloud alternative with OPA policy enforcement and hierarchical configs. *Avoid when* Atlantis or native CI pipelines suffice.
summary: Terraform automation and collaboration software.
use_when: You need a Terraform Cloud alternative with OPA policy enforcement and hierarchical configs.

avoid_when: Budget is limited and simpler tooling covers your workflow.
name: Spacelift
raw:
- [Spacelift](https://spacelift.io/) - IaC automation with policy-as-code and collaboration.
    - *Use when* you need enterprise-grade IaC orchestration with multi-tool support (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation). *Avoid when* budget is limited and simpler tooling covers your workflow.
summary: IaC automation with policy-as-code and collaboration.
use_when: You need enterprise-grade IaC orchestration with multi-tool support (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation).

avoid_when: You want open-source tooling or need to avoid vendor dependency on HashiCorp.
name: Terraform Cloud
raw:
- [Terraform Cloud](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/enterprise/cloud-docs) - Managed service for Terraform workflows and state management.
    - *Use when* you want HashiCorp-managed remote state, runs, and Sentinel policies. *Avoid when* you want open-source tooling or need to avoid vendor dependency on HashiCorp.
summary: Managed service for Terraform workflows and state management.
use_when: You want HashiCorp-managed remote state, runs, and Sentinel policies.

avoid_when: You use GitLab/Bitbucket or prefer a fully self-hosted solution.
name: Terrateam
raw: - [Terrateam](https://terrateam.io/) Open-core / SaaS - GitOps-style Terraform pull-request automation with collaboration features. ([GitHub](https://github.com/terrateamio/terrateam)) - *Use when* you want GitHub-native Terraform automation with access controls and apply locks. *Avoid when* you use GitLab/Bitbucket or prefer a fully self-hosted solution.
summary: GitOps-style Terraform pull-request automation with collaboration features.
use_when: You want GitHub-native Terraform automation with access controls and apply locks.

avoid_when: Musl libc compatibility issues or lack of glibc-based packages blocks your workload.
name: Alpine Linux
raw: - [Alpine Linux](https://www.alpinelinux.org/) OSS - Security-oriented, lightweight Linux distribution. ([GitHub](https://github.com/alpinelinux)) - *Use when* you need tiny container base images with a small attack surface. *Avoid when* musl libc compatibility issues or lack of glibc-based packages blocks your workload.
summary: Security-oriented, lightweight Linux distribution.
use_when: You need tiny container base images with a small attack surface.

avoid_when: You need general-purpose SSH access and package management on the host.
name: Bottlerocket
raw: - [Bottlerocket](https://bottlerocket.dev/) OSS - Linux-based OS for running containers. ([GitHub](https://github.com/bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket)) - *Use when* you want an immutable, security-hardened OS purpose-built for container hosts. *Avoid when* you need general-purpose SSH access and package management on the host.
summary: Linux-based OS for running containers.
use_when: You want an immutable, security-hardened OS purpose-built for container hosts.

avoid_when: You need Docker-CLI-level UX for local development without additional tooling.
name: containerd
raw: - [containerd](https://containerd.io/) OSS - Container runtime. ([GitHub](https://github.com/containerd/containerd)) - *Use when* you need a lightweight, production-grade container runtime (Kubernetes default). *Avoid when* you need Docker-CLI-level UX for local development without additional tooling.
summary: Container runtime.
use_when: You need a lightweight, production-grade container runtime (Kubernetes default).

avoid_when: You also need to run containers outside Kubernetes on the same host.
name: CRI-O
raw: - [CRI-O](https://cri-o.io/) OSS - Kubernetes container runtime (CRI implementation). ([GitHub](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o)) - *Use when* you want a minimal, Kubernetes-only container runtime with no extras. *Avoid when* you also need to run containers outside Kubernetes on the same host.
summary: Kubernetes container runtime (CRI implementation).
use_when: You want a minimal, Kubernetes-only container runtime with no extras.

avoid_when: Your workloads are stateless and easily re-schedulable.
name: CRIU
raw: - [CRIU](https://criu.org/Main_Page) OSS - Checkpoint/Restore In Userspace for Linux containers and processes. ([GitHub](https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu)) - *Use when* you need live migration, fast restart, or snapshotting of running processes/containers. *Avoid when* your workloads are stateless and easily re-schedulable.
summary: Checkpoint/Restore In Userspace for Linux containers and processes.
use_when: You need live migration, fast restart, or snapshotting of running processes/containers.

avoid_when: You already have a full monitoring stack (Prometheus/Grafana) in place.
name: ctop
raw: - [ctop](https://ctop.sh/) OSS - Container metrics viewer (top-like). ([GitHub](https://github.com/bcicen/ctop)) - *Use when* you want a quick, visual overview of container resource usage in a terminal. *Avoid when* you already have a full monitoring stack (Prometheus/Grafana) in place.
summary: Container metrics viewer (top-like).
use_when: You want a quick, visual overview of container resource usage in a terminal.

avoid_when: You don't need image optimization or already use multi-stage builds effectively.
name: dive
raw: - [dive](https://github.com/wagoodman/dive) OSS - Explore Docker image layers. - *Use when* you want to analyze and reduce Docker image size by inspecting each layer. *Avoid when* you don't need image optimization or already use multi-stage builds effectively.
summary: Explore Docker image layers.
use_when: You want to analyze and reduce Docker image size by inspecting each layer.

avoid_when: Licensing costs are a concern for large teams or you prefer open-source alternatives.
name: Docker Desktop
raw:
- [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) - Desktop Docker environment.
    - *Use when* you want a batteries-included Docker experience on Mac/Windows with GUI. *Avoid when* licensing costs are a concern for large teams or you prefer open-source alternatives.
summary: Desktop Docker environment.
use_when: You want a batteries-included Docker experience on Mac/Windows with GUI.

avoid_when: You need production-grade macOS VMs or strict Apple EULA compliance.
name: Dockur macOS
raw: - [Dockur macOS](https://github.com/dockur/macos) OSS - macOS in a Docker container. - *Use when* you need a macOS environment for CI/testing without dedicated Apple hardware. *Avoid when* you need production-grade macOS VMs or strict Apple EULA compliance.
summary: MacOS in a Docker container.
use_when: You need a macOS environment for CI/testing without dedicated Apple hardware.

avoid_when: You need production Windows workloads with full licensing compliance.
name: Dockur Windows
raw: - [Dockur Windows](https://github.com/dockur/windows) OSS - Windows in a Docker container. - *Use when* you need a disposable Windows environment for testing or CI. *Avoid when* you need production Windows workloads with full licensing compliance.
summary: Windows in a Docker container.
use_when: You need a disposable Windows environment for testing or CI.

avoid_when: You need full VM features like GPU passthrough or legacy OS support.
name: Firecracker
raw: - [Firecracker](https://firecracker-microvm.github.io/) OSS - Lightweight virtualization for microVMs. ([GitHub](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker)) - *Use when* you need sub-second VM startup for multi-tenant serverless or container workloads. *Avoid when* you need full VM features like GPU passthrough or legacy OS support.
summary: Lightweight virtualization for microVMs.
use_when: You need sub-second VM startup for multi-tenant serverless or container workloads.

avoid_when: You need to install arbitrary packages or run non-containerized workloads.
name: Flatcar Container Linux
raw: - [Flatcar Container Linux](https://www.flatcar.org/) OSS - Immutable Linux distro for containers. ([GitHub](https://github.com/flatcar/Flatcar)) - *Use when* you want an auto-updating, immutable OS for container hosts. *Avoid when* you need to install arbitrary packages or run non-containerized workloads.
summary: Immutable Linux distro for containers.
use_when: You want an auto-updating, immutable OS for container hosts.

avoid_when: You only need application containers (Docker/Podman) or full hypervisor features.
name: Incus
raw: - [Incus](https://linuxcontainers.org/fr/incus/introduction/) OSS - Modern system container and VM manager. ([GitHub](https://github.com/lxc/incus)) - *Use when* you want a unified tool for system containers and VMs with a modern API. *Avoid when* you only need application containers (Docker/Podman) or full hypervisor features.
summary: Modern system container and VM manager.
use_when: You want a unified tool for system containers and VMs with a modern API.

avoid_when: The performance overhead of micro-VMs is unacceptable or you run trusted workloads only.
name: Kata Containers
raw: - [Kata Containers](https://katacontainers.io/) OSS - Secure containers with lightweight VMs. ([GitHub](https://github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers)) - *Use when* you need VM-level isolation for untrusted container workloads. *Avoid when* the performance overhead of micro-VMs is unacceptable or you run trusted workloads only.
summary: Secure containers with lightweight VMs.
use_when: You need VM-level isolation for untrusted container workloads.

avoid_when: You prefer scripted automation or already use Portainer.
name: Lazydocker
raw: - [Lazydocker](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazydocker) OSS - Terminal UI for Docker and Docker Compose. - *Use when* you want a quick TUI to manage containers, images, and logs without memorizing CLI flags. *Avoid when* you prefer scripted automation or already use Portainer.
summary: Terminal UI for Docker and Docker Compose.
use_when: You want a quick TUI to manage containers, images, and logs without memorizing CLI flags.

avoid_when: You only run containers or use a higher-level orchestrator like Proxmox.
name: libvirt
raw: - [libvirt](https://libvirt.org/) OSS - API/daemon for managing virtualization platforms. ([GitHub](https://github.com/libvirt/libvirt)) - *Use when* you need a stable abstraction layer over KVM/QEMU/Xen for VM management. *Avoid when* you only run containers or use a higher-level orchestrator like Proxmox.
summary: API/daemon for managing virtualization platforms.
use_when: You need a stable abstraction layer over KVM/QEMU/Xen for VM management.

avoid_when: You're on Linux or prefer a more integrated solution like OrbStack.
name: Lima
raw: - [Lima](https://lima-vm.io/) OSS - Linux VMs on macOS (and more). ([GitHub](https://github.com/lima-vm/lima)) - *Use when* you need lightweight Linux VMs on macOS for container development without Docker Desktop. *Avoid when* you're on Linux or prefer a more integrated solution like OrbStack.
summary: Linux VMs on macOS (and more).
use_when: You need lightweight Linux VMs on macOS for container development without Docker Desktop.

avoid_when: You need OCI-compliant application containers for microservices.
name: Linux Containers (LXC/LXD)
raw: - [Linux Containers (LXC/LXD)](https://linuxcontainers.org/) OSS - System containers and VM manager. ([GitHub](https://github.com/canonical/lxd)) - *Use when* you want lightweight system containers that behave like VMs. *Avoid when* you need OCI-compliant application containers for microservices.
summary: System containers and VM manager.
use_when: You want lightweight system containers that behave like VMs.

avoid_when: You need full API parity with AWS or are testing non-AWS services.
name: LocalStack
raw: - [LocalStack](https://www.localstack.cloud/) Open-core / SaaS - Local AWS cloud emulator for development and testing. ([GitHub](https://github.com/localstack/localstack)) - *Use when* you want to develop and test AWS integrations offline without incurring cloud costs. *Avoid when* you need full API parity with AWS or are testing non-AWS services.
summary: Local AWS cloud emulator for development and testing.
use_when: You want to develop and test AWS integrations offline without incurring cloud costs.

avoid_when: You're already using Docker or Podman and don't want to switch.
name: nerdctl
raw: - [nerdctl](https://github.com/containerd/nerdctl) OSS - Docker-compatible CLI for containerd. - *Use when* you want a Docker-like CLI experience on top of containerd without Docker daemon. *Avoid when* you're already using Docker or Podman and don't want to switch.
summary: Docker-compatible CLI for containerd.
use_when: You want a Docker-like CLI experience on top of containerd without Docker daemon.

avoid_when: You need cross-platform support or a fully open-source tool.
name: OrbStack
raw:
- [OrbStack](https://orbstack.dev/) - Fast Docker & Linux VM environment for macOS.

summary: Fast Docker & Linux VM environment for macOS.
use_when: You want a faster, lower-resource Docker Desktop alternative on macOS.

avoid_when: Docker Compose ecosystem compatibility (especially on macOS) is a hard requirement.
name: Podman
raw: - [Podman](https://podman.io/) OSS - Daemonless container engine for developing and managing containers. ([GitHub](https://github.com/containers/podman)) - *Use when* you want rootless, daemonless containers with Docker CLI compatibility. *Avoid when* Docker Compose ecosystem compatibility (especially on macOS) is a hard requirement.
summary: Daemonless container engine for developing and managing containers.
use_when: You want rootless, daemonless containers with Docker CLI compatibility.

avoid_when: You need GitOps-style declarative management or are already using a full platform.
name: Portainer
raw: - [Portainer](https://www.portainer.io/) Open-core / SaaS - Container management platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/portainer/portainer)) - *Use when* you want a web UI to manage Docker/Kubernetes for small teams or edge environments. *Avoid when* you need GitOps-style declarative management or are already using a full platform.
summary: Container management platform.
use_when: You want a web UI to manage Docker/Kubernetes for small teams or edge environments.

avoid_when: You run a single Proxmox node or prefer cloud-based orchestration.
name: Proxmox Datacenter Manager
raw:
- [Proxmox Datacenter Manager](https://www.proxmox.com/en/products/proxmox-datacenter-manager/overview) - Proxmox datacenter management product.

summary: Proxmox datacenter management product.
use_when: You operate multiple Proxmox clusters and need centralized management.

avoid_when: You need VMware-level enterprise support or advanced vSAN features.

raw: - [Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE)](https://www.proxmox.com/en/products/proxmox-virtual-environment/overview) Open-core / SaaS - Open source virtualization platform (KVM + LXC) with optional enterprise subscription. ([GitHub](https://github.com/proxmox)) - *Use when* you want a powerful, free hypervisor with a web UI for on-prem VMs and containers. *Avoid when* you need VMware-level enterprise support or advanced vSAN features.
summary: Open source virtualization platform (KVM + LXC) with optional enterprise subscription.
use_when: You want a powerful, free hypervisor with a web UI for on-prem VMs and containers.

avoid_when: You prefer manual tuning or use a different hypervisor.
name: proxmox-optimizer
raw: - [proxmox-optimizer](https://github.com/dtouzeau/proxmox-optimizer) OSS - Proxmox optimization utilities. - *Use when* you want quick tuning scripts for Proxmox performance. *Avoid when* you prefer manual tuning or use a different hypervisor.
summary: Proxmox optimization utilities.
use_when: You want quick tuning scripts for Proxmox performance.

avoid_when: You don't need local Kubernetes and just want a simple Docker environment.
name: Rancher Desktop
raw: - [Rancher Desktop](https://rancherdesktop.io/) OSS - Desktop Kubernetes and container management. ([GitHub](https://github.com/rancher-sandbox/rancher-desktop)) - *Use when* you want a free, open-source Docker Desktop alternative with built-in K8s. *Avoid when* you don't need local Kubernetes and just want a simple Docker environment.
summary: Desktop Kubernetes and container management.
use_when: You want a free, open-source Docker Desktop alternative with built-in K8s.

avoid_when: You primarily use macOS/Windows with their built-in remote tools.

raw: - [Remmina](https://remmina.org/) OSS - Remote desktop client. ([GitHub](https://github.com/FreeRDP/Remmina)) - *Use when* you need a Linux-native RDP/VNC/SSH remote desktop client. *Avoid when* you primarily use macOS/Windows with their built-in remote tools.
summary: Remote desktop client.
use_when: You need a Linux-native RDP/VNC/SSH remote desktop client.

avoid_when: You're an end-user—tools like Podman/Docker already integrate this.

raw: - [RootlessKit](https://github.com/rootless-containers/rootlesskit) OSS - Rootless container toolkit. - *Use when* you're building rootless container runtimes and need user namespace plumbing. *Avoid when* you're an end-user—tools like Podman/Docker already integrate this.
summary: Rootless container toolkit.
use_when: You're building rootless container runtimes and need user namespace plumbing.

use_when: You need the reference OCI container runtime (used by Docker, containerd, CRI-O).

avoid_when: You need granular control over cluster bootstrapping or use managed K8s.
name: Sealos
raw: - [Sealos](https://sealos.io/) OSS - Cloud operating system for Kubernetes. summary: Cloud operating system for Kubernetes.
use_when: You want a one-click Kubernetes cluster lifecycle manager with app marketplace.

name: Sustainable Computing (Kepler)
raw: - [Sustainable Computing (Kepler)](https://sustainable-computing.io/) OSS - Power consumption monitoring for Kubernetes (project ecosystem). ([GitHub](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler)) - *Use when* you want to measure and optimize energy consumption of Kubernetes workloads. *Avoid when* energy monitoring isn't a priority or your infra lacks eBPF/hardware power counters.
summary: Power consumption monitoring for Kubernetes (project ecosystem).
use_when: You want to measure and optimize energy consumption of Kubernetes workloads.

avoid_when: You need enterprise storage features or a free/open-source solution.
name: Unraid
raw:
- [Unraid](https://unraid.net/) - Operating system for network-attached storage and virtualization.
    - *Use when* you want an easy-to-use home/prosumer NAS+VM platform with a plugin ecosystem. *Avoid when* you need enterprise storage features or a free/open-source solution.
summary: Operating system for network-attached storage and virtualization.
use_when: You want an easy-to-use home/prosumer NAS+VM platform with a plugin ecosystem.

avoid_when: Your volumes are provisioned by CSI drivers or init containers suffice.
name: Volare
raw: - [Volare](https://github.com/AdamShannag/volare) OSS - Kubernetes volume populator that populates Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) from multiple external sources concurrently. - *Use when* you need to pre-populate PVCs from multiple sources (S3, Git, HTTP) before pod startup. *Avoid when* your volumes are provisioned by CSI drivers or init containers suffice.
summary: Kubernetes volume populator that populates Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) from multiple external sources concurrently.
use_when: You need to pre-populate PVCs from multiple sources (S3, Git, HTTP) before pod startup.

avoid_when: You prefer KVM-based virtualization or need broad community/third-party tooling.
name: XCP-ng
raw: - [XCP-ng](https://xcp-ng.org/) OSS - Open-source virtualization platform (Xen-based). ([GitHub](https://github.com/xcp-ng)) - *Use when* you want a fully open-source Xen hypervisor with Xen Orchestra management. *Avoid when* you prefer KVM-based virtualization or need broad community/third-party tooling.
summary: Open-source virtualization platform (Xen-based).
use_when: You want a fully open-source Xen hypervisor with Xen Orchestra management.

avoid_when: You only need simple message queuing (consider RabbitMQ or SQS instead).
name: Apache Kafka
raw: - [Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/) OSS - Distributed event streaming platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/apache/kafka)) - *Use when* you need durable, high-throughput event streaming with replay capability. *Avoid when* you only need simple message queuing (consider RabbitMQ or SQS instead).
summary: Distributed event streaming platform.
use_when: You need durable, high-throughput event streaming with replay capability.

avoid_when: You need OLTP workloads, frequent small updates, or strong transactional guarantees.
name: ClickHouse
raw: - [ClickHouse](https://clickhouse.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Columnar database for analytics. ([GitHub](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse)) - *Use when* you need blazing-fast OLAP queries on large datasets. *Avoid when* you need OLTP workloads, frequent small updates, or strong transactional guarantees.
summary: Columnar database for analytics.
use_when: You need blazing-fast OLAP queries on large datasets.

avoid_when: You need enterprise-grade performance or a mature ecosystem.
name: Garage
raw: - [Garage](https://garagehq.deuxfleurs.fr/) OSS - Lightweight S3-compatible object storage. ([Source](https://git.deuxfleurs.fr/Deuxfleurs/garage)) - *Use when* you want a self-hosted, geo-distributed S3-compatible store with minimal resources. *Avoid when* you need enterprise-grade performance or a mature ecosystem.
summary: Lightweight S3-compatible object storage.
use_when: You want a self-hosted, geo-distributed S3-compatible store with minimal resources.

avoid_when: You manage Garage via CLI/API or use a different object store.
name: Garage WebUI
raw:
- [Garage WebUI](https://hub.docker.com/r/khairul169/garage-webui) - Web interface for Garage object storage.
    - *Use when* you run Garage and want a simple browser-based management UI. *Avoid when* you manage Garage via CLI/API or use a different object store.
summary: Web interface for Garage object storage.
use_when: You run Garage and want a simple browser-based management UI.

avoid_when: You don't need POSIX semantics or your workload fits a simple object store.
name: JuiceFS
raw: - [JuiceFS](https://juicefs.com/en/) Open-core / SaaS - Distributed POSIX file system with community edition and enterprise/cloud offerings. ([GitHub](https://github.com/juicedata/juicefs)) - *Use when* you need a POSIX-compatible distributed filesystem backed by object storage. *Avoid when* you don't need POSIX semantics or your workload fits a simple object store.
summary: Distributed POSIX file system with community edition and enterprise/cloud offerings.
use_when: You need a POSIX-compatible distributed filesystem backed by object storage.

avoid_when: You need persistence, data structures, or pub/sub (use Redis instead).
name: Memcached
raw: - [Memcached](https://memcached.org/) OSS - High-performance, distributed memory object caching system. - *Use when* you need dead-simple, high-speed key-value caching with minimal overhead. *Avoid when* you need persistence, data structures, or pub/sub (use Redis instead).
summary: High-performance, distributed memory object caching system.
use_when: You need dead-simple, high-speed key-value caching with minimal overhead.

avoid_when: The AGPL license or enterprise pricing doesn't fit your model.
name: MinIO
raw: - [MinIO](https://www.min.io/) Open-core / SaaS - High-performance object storage. ([GitHub](https://github.com/minio/minio)) - *Use when* you need S3-compatible object storage on-prem with high throughput. *Avoid when* the AGPL license or enterprise pricing doesn't fit your model.
summary: High-performance object storage.
use_when: You need S3-compatible object storage on-prem with high throughput.

avoid_when: You need disk-first durability or the license change affects your distribution model.
name: Redis
raw: - [Redis](https://redis.io/) OSS Source-available - In-memory data structure store, used as a database, cache, and message broker. **Licensing varies by version:** Redis ≤7.2 uses BSD (OSS); Redis CE 7.4–7.8 uses RSAL/SSPL (source-available); Redis 8+ uses tri-license (AGPL option available). ([GitHub](https://github.com/redis/redis)) - *Use when* you need an in-memory store with rich data structures, pub/sub, and Lua scripting. *Avoid when* you need disk-first durability or the license change affects your distribution model.
summary: In-memory data structure store, used as a database, cache, and message broker. **Licensing varies by version:** Redis ≤7.2 uses BSD (OSS); Redis CE 7.4–7.8 uses RSAL/SSPL (source-available); Redis 8+ uses tri-license (AGPL option available).
use_when: You need an in-memory store with rich data structures, pub/sub, and Lua scripting.

avoid_when: You need a battle-tested storage system for production-critical data.
name: RustFS
raw: - [RustFS](https://rustfs.com/) OSS - S3-compatible object storage system implemented in Rust. ([GitHub](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs)) - *Use when* you want a modern, Rust-based S3-compatible store with memory safety guarantees. *Avoid when* you need a battle-tested storage system for production-critical data.
summary: S3-compatible object storage system implemented in Rust.
use_when: You want a modern, Rust-based S3-compatible store with memory safety guarantees.

avoid_when: You only need simple object storage and want a larger community (use MinIO).
name: SeaweedFS
raw: - [SeaweedFS](https://seaweedfs.com/) OSS - Distributed storage system for files, objects, and volumes. ([GitHub](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs)) - *Use when* you need a fast distributed filesystem that also speaks S3 and supports tiered storage. *Avoid when* you only need simple object storage and want a larger community (use MinIO).
summary: Distributed storage system for files, objects, and volumes.
use_when: You need a fast distributed filesystem that also speaks S3 and supports tiered storage.

avoid_when: You only need a reverse proxy/load balancer (use Nginx/HAProxy instead).
name: Squid
raw: - [Squid](https://www.squid-cache.org/) OSS - Caching proxy for the web (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and more). - *Use when* you need a forward/reverse caching proxy to reduce bandwidth and speed up web content. *Avoid when* you only need a reverse proxy/load balancer (use Nginx/HAProxy instead).
summary: Caching proxy for the web (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and more).
use_when: You need a forward/reverse caching proxy to reduce bandwidth and speed up web content.

avoid_when: You're fully in the cloud or not using AWS.
name: AWS Storage Gateway
raw:
- [AWS Storage Gateway](https://aws.amazon.com/fr/storagegateway/) - Hybrid cloud storage service.
    - *Use when* you need to bridge on-prem storage with AWS (file, volume, or tape gateway). *Avoid when* you're fully in the cloud or not using AWS.
summary: Hybrid cloud storage service.
use_when: You need to bridge on-prem storage with AWS (file, volume, or tape gateway).

avoid_when: You're migrating infrastructure rather than user files.
name: CloudFuze
raw:
- [CloudFuze](https://www.cloudfuze.com/) - Cloud file transfer and management.
    - *Use when* you need to migrate files between cloud storage providers (OneDrive, Google Drive, etc.). *Avoid when* you're migrating infrastructure rather than user files.
summary: Cloud file transfer and management.
use_when: You need to migrate files between cloud storage providers (OneDrive, Google Drive, etc.).

avoid_when: Your workloads are single-cloud with built-in cost tools.
name: Concierto Cloud
raw:
- [Concierto Cloud](https://www.concierto.cloud/) - Cloud management platform.
    - *Use when* you need a unified dashboard for multi-cloud governance and cost optimization. *Avoid when* your workloads are single-cloud with built-in cost tools.
summary: Cloud management platform.
use_when: You need a unified dashboard for multi-cloud governance and cost optimization.

avoid_when: You're cloud-native with existing IaC pipelines.
name: Morpheus Data
raw:
- [Morpheus Data](https://morpheusdata.com/) - Hybrid cloud management platform.
    - *Use when* you need a single pane of glass for provisioning across private and public clouds. *Avoid when* you're cloud-native with existing IaC pipelines.
summary: Hybrid cloud management platform.
use_when: You need a single pane of glass for provisioning across private and public clouds.

avoid_when: Your monitoring and capacity needs are already covered by existing tools.
name: Virtana
raw:
- [Virtana](https://www.virtana.com/) - Hybrid cloud management.
    - *Use when* you need AI-driven infrastructure performance and capacity planning across hybrid environments. *Avoid when* your monitoring and capacity needs are already covered by existing tools.
summary: Hybrid cloud management.
use_when: You need AI-driven infrastructure performance and capacity planning across hybrid environments.

avoid_when: * Your workloads are primarily backend or non-mobile.
name: Appcircle
raw:
- [Appcircle](https://appcircle.io/) - CI/CD platform for mobile apps.
    - *Use when:* You need a dedicated mobile CI/CD with native iOS/Android build support. *Avoid when:* Your workloads are primarily backend or non-mobile.
summary: CI/CD platform for mobile apps.
use_when: * You need a dedicated mobile CI/CD with native iOS/Android build support.

avoid_when: * You don't have Kubernetes or need a simple, linear CI pipeline.
name: Argo Workflows
raw: - [Argo Workflows](https://argoproj.github.io/argo-workflows/) OSS - Kubernetes-native workflow engine. ([GitHub](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows)) - *Use when:* You already run Kubernetes and need DAG-based pipelines for complex workflows. *Avoid when:* You don't have Kubernetes or need a simple, linear CI pipeline.
summary: Kubernetes-native workflow engine.
use_when: * You already run Kubernetes and need DAG-based pipelines for complex workflows.

avoid_when: * You prefer open tooling or are multi-cloud without Azure ties.
name: Azure DevOps
raw:
- [Azure DevOps](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/devops/) - Microsoft's DevOps platform.
    - *Use when:* You're invested in the Microsoft/Azure ecosystem and want integrated boards, repos, and pipelines. *Avoid when:* You prefer open tooling or are multi-cloud without Azure ties.
summary: Microsoft's DevOps platform.
use_when: * You're invested in the Microsoft/Azure ecosystem and want integrated boards, repos, and pipelines.

avoid_when: * You want a cloud-native or actively-evolving CI/CD (Atlassian is sunsetting Bamboo in favor of Bitbucket Pipelines).
name: Bamboo
raw:
- [Bamboo](https://www.atlassian.com/software/bamboo) - CI/CD server by Atlassian.
    - *Use when:* You're deep in the Atlassian stack (Jira, Bitbucket). *Avoid when:* You want a cloud-native or actively-evolving CI/CD (Atlassian is sunsetting Bamboo in favor of Bitbucket Pipelines).
summary: CI/CD server by Atlassian.
use_when: * You're deep in the Atlassian stack (Jira, Bitbucket).

avoid_when: * You need complex multi-repo or multi-cloud pipelines.
name: Bitbucket Pipelines
raw:
- [Bitbucket Pipelines](https://www.atlassian.com/software/bitbucket/features/pipelines) - Integrated CI/CD for Bitbucket repositories.
    - *Use when:* Your source code lives in Bitbucket and you want zero-config CI. *Avoid when:* You need complex multi-repo or multi-cloud pipelines.
summary: Integrated CI/CD for Bitbucket repositories.
use_when: * Your source code lives in Bitbucket and you want zero-config CI.

avoid_when: * Your projects are server-side or infrastructure-focused.
name: Bitrise
raw:
- [Bitrise](https://bitrise.io/) - CI/CD for mobile apps with automation workflows. ([GitHub](https://github.com/bitrise-io))
    - *Use when:* You build mobile apps and want pre-built integrations for iOS/Android. *Avoid when:* Your projects are server-side or infrastructure-focused.
summary: CI/CD for mobile apps with automation workflows.
use_when: * You build mobile apps and want pre-built integrations for iOS/Android.

avoid_when: * You need enterprise-grade scale or complex orchestration.
name: Buddy
raw:
- [Buddy](https://buddy.works/) - CI/CD pipeline automation tool.
    - *Use when:* You want a visual, low-config CI/CD for web projects. *Avoid when:* You need enterprise-grade scale or complex orchestration.
summary: CI/CD pipeline automation tool.
use_when: * You want a visual, low-config CI/CD for web projects.

avoid_when: * You prefer fully managed builds and don't want to manage agents.
name: Buildkite
raw:
- [Buildkite](https://buildkite.com/) - CI/CD platform with agent-based execution.
    - *Use when:* You want to run builds on your own infrastructure with a managed orchestration layer. *Avoid when:* You prefer fully managed builds and don't want to manage agents.
summary: CI/CD platform with agent-based execution.
use_when: * You want to run builds on your own infrastructure with a managed orchestration layer.

avoid_when: * You need a battle-tested platform with a large ecosystem of plugins and integrations.
name: Cadence CI
raw:
- [Cadence CI](https://cadence.ci/) - CI/CD platform.
    - *Use when:* You need a lightweight CI/CD solution. *Avoid when:* You need a battle-tested platform with a large ecosystem of plugins and integrations.
summary: CI/CD platform.
use_when: * You need a lightweight CI/CD solution.

avoid_when: * You need on-prem-only execution or strict data residency.
name: CircleCI
raw:
- [CircleCI](https://circleci.com/) - Cloud CI/CD platform.
    - *Use when:* You want fast, cloud-hosted CI with excellent caching and parallelism. *Avoid when:* You need on-prem-only execution or strict data residency.
summary: Cloud CI/CD platform.
use_when: * You want fast, cloud-hosted CI with excellent caching and parallelism.

avoid_when: * You want to avoid Jenkins complexity or vendor lock-in.
name: CloudBees
raw: - [CloudBees](https://www.cloudbees.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Enterprise CI/CD built around Jenkins. - *Use when:* You need enterprise Jenkins with governance, RBAC, and support. *Avoid when:* You want to avoid Jenkins complexity or vendor lock-in.
summary: Enterprise CI/CD built around Jenkins.
use_when: * You need enterprise Jenkins with governance, RBAC, and support.

avoid_when: * You only need simple CI with no Kubernetes component.
name: Codefresh
raw:
- [Codefresh](https://codefresh.io/) - GitOps and CI/CD platform.
    - *Use when:* You want combined CI/CD + GitOps (ArgoCD-based) in a single platform. *Avoid when:* You only need simple CI with no Kubernetes component.
summary: GitOps and CI/CD platform.
use_when: * You want combined CI/CD + GitOps (ArgoCD-based) in a single platform.

avoid_when: * You need a quick setup with lots of community plugins; the learning curve is steep.
name: Concourse
raw: - [Concourse](https://concourse-ci.org/) OSS - CI/CD system with declarative pipelines. ([GitHub](https://github.com/concourse/concourse)) - *Use when:* You want truly reproducible, declarative pipelines with resource-based semantics. *Avoid when:* You need a quick setup with lots of community plugins; the learning curve is steep.
summary: CI/CD system with declarative pipelines.
use_when: * You want truly reproducible, declarative pipelines with resource-based semantics.

avoid_when: * Your team prefers YAML-based pipelines or isn't comfortable with programmatic pipeline definitions.
name: Dagger
raw: - [Dagger](https://dagger.io/) OSS - CI/CD as code toolkit. ([GitHub](https://github.com/dagger/dagger)) - *Use when:* You want portable, container-native pipelines that run identically locally and in any CI. *Avoid when:* Your team prefers YAML-based pipelines or isn't comfortable with programmatic pipeline definitions.
summary: CI/CD as code toolkit.
use_when: * You want portable, container-native pipelines that run identically locally and in any CI.

avoid_when: * You need enterprise features (now largely folded into Harness).
name: Drone
raw: - [Drone](https://www.drone.io/) OSS - Container-native CI/CD platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/harness/drone)) - *Use when:* You want a lightweight, container-first CI with simple YAML config. *Avoid when:* You need enterprise features (now largely folded into Harness).
summary: Container-native CI/CD platform.
use_when: * You want a lightweight, container-first CI with simple YAML config.

avoid_when: * You need full control over runner infrastructure or are not on GitHub.
name: GitHub Actions
raw:
- [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/features/actions) - CI/CD automation built into GitHub.
    - *Use when:* Your code is on GitHub and you want frictionless CI/CD with a massive marketplace. *Avoid when:* You need full control over runner infrastructure or are not on GitHub.
summary: CI/CD automation built into GitHub.
use_when: * Your code is on GitHub and you want frictionless CI/CD with a massive marketplace.

avoid_when: * You don't use GitLab, or you need a CI-only tool without the full platform.
name: GitLab CI
raw: - [GitLab CI](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/) Open-core / SaaS - CI/CD built into GitLab. - *Use when:* You use GitLab for SCM and want a single platform for code, CI/CD, and security scanning. *Avoid when:* You don't use GitLab, or you need a CI-only tool without the full platform.
summary: CI/CD built into GitLab.
use_when: * You use GitLab for SCM and want a single platform for code, CI/CD, and security scanning.

avoid_when: * You want a large plugin ecosystem or cloud-native integrations.
name: GoCD
raw: - [GoCD](https://www.gocd.org/) OSS - Open-source CI/CD server. ([GitHub](https://github.com/gocd/gocd)) - *Use when:* You need advanced pipeline modeling (fan-in/fan-out, value stream maps). *Avoid when:* You want a large plugin ecosystem or cloud-native integrations.
summary: Open-source CI/CD server.
use_when: * You need advanced pipeline modeling (fan-in/fan-out, value stream maps).

avoid_when: * You're multi-cloud or need on-prem build execution.
name: Google Cloud Build
raw:
- [Google Cloud Build](https://cloud.google.com/build) - CI/CD service for Google Cloud.
    - *Use when:* You're on GCP and want a serverless, pay-per-build CI service. *Avoid when:* You're multi-cloud or need on-prem build execution.
summary: CI/CD service for Google Cloud.
use_when: * You're on GCP and want a serverless, pay-per-build CI service.

avoid_when: * You want a simple, lightweight CI or prefer OSS-only tooling.
name: Harness
raw:
- [Harness](https://harness.io/) - CI/CD and DevOps platform.
    - *Use when:* You want an enterprise platform covering CI, CD, feature flags, and cost management. *Avoid when:* You want a simple, lightweight CI or prefer OSS-only tooling.
summary: CI/CD and DevOps platform.
use_when: * You want an enterprise platform covering CI, CD, feature flags, and cost management.

avoid_when: * You don't want to maintain infrastructure, manage plugin compatibility, or deal with Groovy DSL complexity.
name: Jenkins
raw: - [Jenkins](https://www.jenkins.io/) OSS - Automation server for CI/CD. ([GitHub](https://github.com/jenkinsci/jenkins)) - *Use when:* You need maximum flexibility with 1,800+ plugins and full self-hosted control. *Avoid when:* You don't want to maintain infrastructure, manage plugin compatibility, or deal with Groovy DSL complexity.
summary: Automation server for CI/CD.
use_when: * You need maximum flexibility with 1,800+ plugins and full self-hosted control.

avoid_when: * You don't run Kubernetes or want fine-grained pipeline control; community activity has slowed.
name: Jenkins X
raw: - [Jenkins X](https://jenkins-x.io/) OSS - Kubernetes-native CI/CD. ([GitHub](https://github.com/jenkins-x/jx)) - *Use when:* You want opinionated, GitOps-driven CI/CD on Kubernetes with automated environments. *Avoid when:* You don't run Kubernetes or want fine-grained pipeline control; community activity has slowed.
summary: Kubernetes-native CI/CD.
use_when: * You want opinionated, GitOps-driven CI/CD on Kubernetes with automated environments.

avoid_when: * You need a full CI/CD pipeline; Keptn augments delivery rather than replacing CI.
name: Keptn
raw: - [Keptn](https://keptn.sh/) OSS - Cloud-native lifecycle management and delivery. ([GitHub](https://github.com/keptn/keptn)) - *Use when:* You need automated quality gates and SLO-based delivery orchestration. *Avoid when:* You need a full CI/CD pipeline; Keptn augments delivery rather than replacing CI.
summary: Cloud-native lifecycle management and delivery.
use_when: * You need automated quality gates and SLO-based delivery orchestration.

avoid_when: * Your workloads are traditional application builds.
name: Mantis
raw: - [Mantis](https://mantis.getaugur.ai/docs/introduction/overview/) OSS - CI/CD platform for ML and data workflows. ([GitHub](https://github.com/augur-ai/mantis)) - *Use when:* You're building ML/data pipelines and want CI/CD tailored to that domain. *Avoid when:* Your workloads are traditional application builds.
summary: CI/CD platform for ML and data workflows.
use_when: * You're building ML/data pipelines and want CI/CD tailored to that domain.

avoid_when: * You don't use GitHub Actions, or your workflows depend heavily on GitHub-hosted runner features.
name: Nektos Act
raw: - [Nektos Act](https://nektosact.com/) OSS - Run GitHub Actions locally. ([GitHub](https://github.com/nektos/act)) - *Use when:* You want to test and debug GitHub Actions workflows locally before pushing. *Avoid when:* You don't use GitHub Actions, or your workflows depend heavily on GitHub-hosted runner features.
summary: Run GitHub Actions locally.
use_when: * You want to test and debug GitHub Actions workflows locally before pushing.

avoid_when: * You only need CI (Octopus focuses on CD) or you're fully Kubernetes-native.
name: Octopus Deploy
raw:
- [Octopus Deploy](https://octopus.com/) - Deployment automation platform.
    - *Use when:* You need release management and deployment orchestration across multiple environments. *Avoid when:* You only need CI (Octopus focuses on CD) or you're fully Kubernetes-native.
summary: Deployment automation platform.
use_when: * You need release management and deployment orchestration across multiple environments.

avoid_when: * You're not on OpenShift; use plain Tekton instead.
name: OpenShift Pipelines
raw:
- [OpenShift Pipelines](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/openshift/pipelines) - Tekton-based CI/CD experience packaged and supported for OpenShift clusters (built on OSS Tekton).
    - *Use when:* You run OpenShift and want integrated, supported Tekton pipelines. *Avoid when:* You're not on OpenShift; use plain Tekton instead.
summary: Tekton-based CI/CD experience packaged and supported for OpenShift clusters (built on OSS Tekton).
use_when: * You run OpenShift and want integrated, supported Tekton pipelines.

avoid_when: * You need heavy on-prem or self-hosted capabilities.
name: Semaphore CI
raw:
- [Semaphore CI](https://semaphoreci.com/) - CI/CD platform for software projects.
    - *Use when:* You want fast, parallelized cloud CI with a clean UI. *Avoid when:* You need heavy on-prem or self-hosted capabilities.
summary: CI/CD platform for software projects.
use_when: * You want fast, parallelized cloud CI with a clean UI.

avoid_when: * You have a single small cluster; Spinnaker's operational overhead is significant.
name: Spinnaker
raw: - [Spinnaker](https://spinnaker.io/) OSS - Multi-cloud continuous delivery platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/spinnaker/spinnaker)) - *Use when:* You deploy across multiple clouds and need advanced deployment strategies (canary, blue/green). *Avoid when:* You have a single small cluster; Spinnaker's operational overhead is significant.
summary: Multi-cloud continuous delivery platform.
use_when: * You deploy across multiple clouds and need advanced deployment strategies (canary, blue/green).

avoid_when: * You prefer pipeline-as-code or need a large open-source plugin ecosystem.
name: TeamCity
raw:
- [TeamCity](https://www.jetbrains.com/teamcity/) - CI/CD server by JetBrains.
    - *Use when:* You use JetBrains IDEs and want deep integration with excellent build configuration UI. *Avoid when:* You prefer pipeline-as-code or need a large open-source plugin ecosystem.
summary: CI/CD server by JetBrains.
use_when: * You use JetBrains IDEs and want deep integration with excellent build configuration UI.

avoid_when: * You don't run Kubernetes or want a batteries-included CI/CD experience.
name: Tekton
raw: - [Tekton](https://tekton.dev/) OSS - Kubernetes-native CI/CD framework. ([GitHub](https://github.com/tektoncd/pipeline)) - *Use when:* You want a composable, Kubernetes-native CI/CD building block. *Avoid when:* You don't run Kubernetes or want a batteries-included CI/CD experience.
summary: Kubernetes-native CI/CD framework.
use_when: * You want a composable, Kubernetes-native CI/CD building block.

avoid_when: * You need enterprise features or high reliability; Travis CI has declined in popularity and investment.
name: Travis CI
raw:
- [Travis CI](https://www.travis-ci.com/) - CI/CD service for GitHub.
    - *Use when:* You want simple CI for open-source projects with minimal config. *Avoid when:* You need enterprise features or high reliability; Travis CI has declined in popularity and investment.
summary: CI/CD service for GitHub.
use_when: * You want simple CI for open-source projects with minimal config.

avoid_when: * You need enterprise support or a large commercial ecosystem.
name: Woodpecker CI
raw: - [Woodpecker CI](https://woodpecker-ci.org/) OSS - CI/CD platform for Git. ([GitHub](https://github.com/woodpecker-ci/woodpecker)) - *Use when:* You want a lightweight, community-driven Drone fork with active development. *Avoid when:* You need enterprise support or a large commercial ecosystem.
summary: CI/CD platform for Git.
use_when: * You want a lightweight, community-driven Drone fork with active development.

avoid_when: * You have a small project; Bazel's complexity is not worth it for simple builds.
name: Bazel
raw: - [Bazel](https://bazel.build/) OSS - Fast, scalable, multi-language build system. ([GitHub](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel)) - *Use when:* You have a large monorepo and need hermetic, incremental builds at scale. *Avoid when:* You have a small project; Bazel's complexity is not worth it for simple builds.
summary: Fast, scalable, multi-language build system.
use_when: * You have a large monorepo and need hermetic, incremental builds at scale.

avoid_when: * You're happy with standard Docker builds and don't have security constraints on the daemon.
name: Buildah
raw: - [Buildah](https://buildah.io/) OSS - Build OCI images without a daemon. ([GitHub](https://github.com/containers/buildah)) - *Use when:* You need daemonless, rootless container image builds (especially in CI or restricted environments). *Avoid when:* You're happy with standard Docker builds and don't have security constraints on the daemon.
summary: Build OCI images without a daemon.
use_when: * You need daemonless, rootless container image builds (especially in CI or restricted environments).

avoid_when: * You're already using it (it's the default in modern Docker); switching only matters on older Docker versions.
name: BuildKit
raw: - [BuildKit](https://docs.docker.com/build/buildkit/) OSS - Next-generation Docker image build engine used by Buildx. ([GitHub](https://github.com/moby/buildkit)) - *Use when:* You want faster Docker builds with better caching, parallelism, and build secrets. *Avoid when:* You're already using it (it's the default in modern Docker); switching only matters on older Docker versions.
summary: Next-generation Docker image build engine used by Buildx.
use_when: * You want faster Docker builds with better caching, parallelism, and build secrets.

avoid_when: * You need to exec into containers for debugging or require OS-level packages at runtime.
name: Distroless
raw: - [Distroless](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/distroless) OSS - Minimal container images for secure deployments. - *Use when:* You want to minimize attack surface by shipping images without shells or package managers. *Avoid when:* You need to exec into containers for debugging or require OS-level packages at runtime.
summary: Minimal container images for secure deployments.
use_when: * You want to minimize attack surface by shipping images without shells or package managers.

avoid_when: * You need daemonless builds or your CI environment doesn't support Docker-in-Docker.

raw:

summary: Docker image build system.
use_when: * You're using Docker and want the standard, well-documented build flow.

summary: Docker CLI plugin for extended build capabilities.
use_when: * You need multi-platform images or advanced BuildKit features via Docker CLI.

summary: Offload Docker builds to the cloud.
use_when: * Local builds are slow and you want to offload compute to the cloud.
