([GitHub](https://github.com/clastix/capsule)) *Use for lightweight, namespace-based multi-tenancy without vClusters; avoid if tenants need full cluster-admin isolation (use vCluster or separate clusters).*
summary: Kubernetes multi-tenancy and policy enforcement.
use_when: Lightweight, namespace-based multi-tenancy without vClusters.

avoid_when: You need infrastructure/K8s admission control (use OPA/Rego).
name: Cedar Policy
raw: - [Cedar Policy](https://www.cedarpolicy.com/en) OSS - Policy language and authorization engine (Cedar) for fine-grained access control. ([GitHub](https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar)) *Use for application-level authorization with a formally verified engine; avoid if you need infrastructure/K8s admission control (use OPA/Rego).*
summary: Policy language and authorization engine (Cedar) for fine-grained access control.
use_when: Application-level authorization with a formally verified engine.

avoid_when: Your kernel doesn't support eBPF or you need a simpler CNI.
name: Cilium
raw: - [Cilium](https://cilium.io/) OSS - eBPF-based networking, observability, and security for Kubernetes. ([GitHub](https://github.com/cilium/cilium)) *Use when you need high-performance, identity-aware network policies with L7 visibility; avoid if your kernel doesn't support eBPF or you need a simpler CNI.*
summary: EBPF-based networking, observability, and security for Kubernetes.
use_when: You need high-performance, identity-aware network policies with L7 visibility.

avoid_when: You're not comfortable writing Rego policies.
name: Conftest
raw: - [Conftest](https://www.conftest.dev/) OSS - Test configuration files using OPA/Rego. ([GitHub](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/conftest)) *Use to shift-left policy checks for Terraform/K8s/Docker configs in CI; avoid if you're not comfortable writing Rego policies.*
summary: Test configuration files using OPA/Rego.
use_when: Shift-left policy checks for Terraform/K8s/Docker configs in CI.

avoid_when: You need deep protocol inspection (use a full IDS like Suricata).
name: CrowdSec
raw: - [CrowdSec](https://www.crowdsec.net/) OSS - Collaborative intrusion prevention/behavior detection engine. ([GitHub](https://github.com/crowdsecurity/crowdsec)) *Use for crowd-sourced IP reputation and behavior-based ban lists; avoid if you need deep protocol inspection (use a full IDS like Suricata).*
summary: Collaborative intrusion prevention/behavior detection engine.
use_when: Crowd-sourced IP reputation and behavior-based ban lists.

avoid_when: For internal or dev certs (use Let's Encrypt or mkcert).
name: DigiCert
raw: - [DigiCert](https://www.digicert.com/) - Digital certificates and SSL solutions. ([GitHub](https://github.com/digicert)) *Use when you need EV/OV certificates with enterprise PKI management; avoid for internal or dev certs (use Let's Encrypt or mkcert).*
summary: Digital certificates and SSL solutions.
use_when: You need EV/OV certificates with enterprise PKI management.

avoid_when: You already have MFA via your IdP (Okta, Azure AD, etc.).
name: Duo Security
raw: - [Duo Security](https://duo.com/) - Multi-factor authentication and access security. *Use for turnkey MFA integration across VPN/SSH/web apps; avoid if you already have MFA via your IdP (Okta, Azure AD, etc.).*
summary: Multi-factor authentication and access security.
use_when: Turnkey MFA integration across VPN/SSH/web apps.

avoid_when: You manage firewall rules declaratively via Ansible/iptables or run in containers.
name: firewalld
raw: - [firewalld](https://firewalld.org/) OSS - Dynamically managed firewall for Linux with D-Bus interface. ([GitHub](https://github.com/firewalld/firewalld)) *Use for dynamic, zone-based host firewall management on RHEL/Fedora; avoid if you manage firewall rules declaratively via Ansible/iptables or run in containers.*
summary: Dynamically managed firewall for Linux with D-Bus interface.
use_when: Dynamic, zone-based host firewall management on RHEL/Fedora.

avoid_when: You're not on GCP or prefer cross-cloud policy tools like OPA.
name: Google Cloud Organization Policy
raw: - [Google Cloud Organization Policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/organization-policy/overview) - GCP resource governance. *Use to enforce constraints across GCP projects/folders; avoid if you're not on GCP or prefer cross-cloud policy tools like OPA.*
summary: GCP resource governance.
use_when: Enforce constraints across GCP projects/folders.

avoid_when: External Secrets or Vault Agent already handle your use case.
name: k8s Sidecar Secret Forge
raw: - [k8s Sidecar Secret Forge](https://github.com/stegianna/k8s-sidecar-secret-forge) OSS - Kubernetes secret management sidecar. *Use for dynamic secret injection without modifying app code; avoid if External Secrets or Vault Agent already handle your use case.*
summary: Kubernetes secret management sidecar.
use_when: Dynamic secret injection without modifying app code.

avoid_when: You need full cluster isolation or use a managed K8s service.
name: Kamaji
raw: - [Kamaji](https://kamaji.clastix.io/) OSS - Kubernetes control plane manager (multi-tenancy/security). ([GitHub](https://github.com/clastix/kamaji)) *Use when you need lightweight, shared-infrastructure tenant control planes; avoid if you need full cluster isolation or use a managed K8s service.*
summary: Kubernetes control plane manager (multi-tenancy/security).
use_when: You need lightweight, shared-infrastructure tenant control planes.

avoid_when: You only need Kubernetes-specific policies (Kyverno may be simpler).
name: Open Policy Agent
raw: - [Open Policy Agent](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/) OSS - Policy-based control for cloud-native environments. ([GitHub](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/opa)) *Use for cross-cutting policy enforcement (K8s admission, API auth, Terraform); avoid if you only need Kubernetes-specific policies (Kyverno may be simpler).*
summary: Policy-based control for cloud-native environments.
use_when: Cross-cutting policy enforcement (K8s admission, API auth, Terraform).

avoid_when: For server workloads or if hardware compatibility is a concern.
name: Qubes OS
raw: - [Qubes OS](https://www.qubes-os.org/) OSS - Security-focused desktop operating system using Xen-based virtualization for compartmentalization. ([GitHub](https://github.com/QubesOS)) *Use when you need strong workstation-level compartmentalization (e.g., security research); avoid for server workloads or if hardware compatibility is a concern.*
summary: Security-focused desktop operating system using Xen-based virtualization for compartmentalization.
use_when: You need strong workstation-level compartmentalization (e.g., security research).

avoid_when: You need Linux-first or cloud-native runtime protection (use Falco).
name: ThreatLocker
raw: - [ThreatLocker](https://www.threatlocker.com/) - Zero trust endpoint protection platform. *Use for allowlist-based endpoint lockdown in regulated environments; avoid if you need Linux-first or cloud-native runtime protection (use Falco).*
summary: Zero trust endpoint protection platform.
use_when: Allowlist-based endpoint lockdown in regulated environments.

avoid_when: You need piecemeal best-of-breed tools or have simple networking needs.
name: Cato Networks
raw: - [Cato Networks](https://www.catonetworks.com/) - SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) platform. *Use for converged SD-WAN + security in distributed enterprises; avoid if you need piecemeal best-of-breed tools or have simple networking needs.*
summary: SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) platform.
use_when: Converged SD-WAN + security in distributed enterprises.

avoid_when: In ephemeral/container environments or if you need crowd-sourced threat intel (use CrowdSec).
name: fail2ban
raw: - [fail2ban](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban) OSS - Intrusion prevention by monitoring logs and banning abusive IPs (e.g., SSH). *Use for simple, log-based brute-force protection on SSH/web servers; avoid in ephemeral/container environments or if you need crowd-sourced threat intel (use CrowdSec).*
summary: Intrusion prevention by monitoring logs and banning abusive IPs (e.g., SSH).
use_when: Simple, log-based brute-force protection on SSH/web servers.

avoid_when: Your infrastructure is fully software-defined or cloud-native.
name: ManageEngine Network Configuration Manager
raw: - [ManageEngine Network Configuration Manager](https://www.manageengine.com/network-configuration-manager/) - Network device configuration management. *Use for managing multi-vendor network device configs with change tracking; avoid if your infrastructure is fully software-defined or cloud-native.*
summary: Network device configuration management.
use_when: Managing multi-vendor network device configs with change tracking.

avoid_when: You need extensive third-party pfSense package ecosystem compatibility.
name: OPNsense
raw: - [OPNsense](https://opnsense.org/) OSS - Open-source firewall and routing software. ([GitHub](https://github.com/opnsense)) *Use for a modern, HardenedBSD-based firewall with frequent updates and a clean UI; avoid if you need extensive third-party pfSense package ecosystem compatibility.*
summary: Open-source firewall and routing software.
use_when: A modern, HardenedBSD-based firewall with frequent updates and a clean UI.

avoid_when: You're concerned about Netgate's licensing direction (consider OPNsense).
name: pfSense
raw: - [pfSense](https://www.pfsense.org/) OSS - Open-source firewall and router platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/pfsense/pfsense)) *Use for a mature, well-documented open-source firewall with a large community; avoid if you're concerned about Netgate's licensing direction (consider OPNsense).*
summary: Open-source firewall and router platform.
use_when: A mature, well-documented open-source firewall with a large community.

avoid_when: You want mesh networking with zero-config (use Tailscale/WireGuard).
name: Pritunl
raw: - [Pritunl](https://pritunl.com/) Open-core / SaaS - VPN server for secure remote access; open-source core with commercial features. ([GitHub](https://github.com/pritunl/pritunl)) *Use for a self-hosted VPN with a web UI and multi-server support; avoid if you want mesh networking with zero-config (use Tailscale/WireGuard).*
summary: VPN server for secure remote access; open-source core with commercial features.
use_when: A self-hosted VPN with a web UI and multi-server support.

avoid_when: You need a traditional gateway VPN or want to avoid a SaaS control plane (use Headscale or WireGuard directly).
name: Tailscale
raw: - [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Zero-config VPN for secure networking; OSS client with commercial/SaaS control plane (self-hosting via Headscale available). ([GitHub](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale)) *Use for zero-config, identity-based mesh networking across devices; avoid if you need a traditional gateway VPN or want to avoid a SaaS control plane (use Headscale or WireGuard directly).*
summary: Zero-config VPN for secure networking; OSS client with commercial/SaaS control plane (self-hosting via Headscale available).
use_when: Zero-config, identity-based mesh networking across devices.

avoid_when: You use External Secrets Operator which covers the same need more broadly.
name: ArgoCD Vault Plugin
raw: - [ArgoCD Vault Plugin](https://argocd-vault-plugin.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) OSS - Integrate secrets with ArgoCD deployments. ([GitHub](https://github.com/argoproj-labs/argocd-vault-plugin)) *Use when you run ArgoCD and want inline secret injection from Vault/AWS SM/etc.; avoid if you use External Secrets Operator which covers the same need more broadly.*
summary: Integrate secrets with ArgoCD deployments.
use_when: You run ArgoCD and want inline secret injection from Vault/AWS SM/etc.

avoid_when: For multi-cloud setups where Vault provides a unified interface.
name: AWS Secrets Manager
raw: - [AWS Secrets Manager](https://aws.amazon.com/secrets-manager/) - Managed secret storage for AWS. *Use for AWS-native workloads needing automatic rotation and IAM-integrated access; avoid for multi-cloud setups where Vault provides a unified interface.*
summary: Managed secret storage for AWS.
use_when: AWS-native workloads needing automatic rotation and IAM-integrated access.

avoid_when: You need self-hosted or air-gapped secret management.
name: Doppler
raw: - [Doppler](https://www.doppler.com/) - Universal secrets management platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/DopplerHQ/cli)) *Use for a SaaS-first, developer-friendly secrets platform across multiple environments; avoid if you need self-hosted or air-gapped secret management.*
summary: Universal secrets management platform.
use_when: A SaaS-first, developer-friendly secrets platform across multiple environments.

avoid_when: Your apps can fetch secrets directly from Vault/cloud APIs.
name: External Secrets
raw: - [External Secrets](https://external-secrets.io/) OSS - Sync external secrets into Kubernetes. ([GitHub](https://github.com/external-secrets/external-secrets)) *Use to sync secrets from any external backend into K8s Secrets declaratively; avoid if your apps can fetch secrets directly from Vault/cloud APIs.*
summary: Sync external secrets into Kubernetes.
use_when: Sync secrets from any external backend into K8s Secrets declaratively.

avoid_when: For simple single-cloud setups where the native secrets manager suffices.
name: HashiCorp Vault
raw: - [HashiCorp Vault](https://www.vaultproject.io/) Source-available - Secure secret storage and access. ([GitHub](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault)) *Use for centralized, multi-cloud secrets with dynamic credentials and encryption-as-a-service; avoid for simple single-cloud setups where the native secrets manager suffices.*
summary: Secure secret storage and access.
use_when: Centralized, multi-cloud secrets with dynamic credentials and encryption-as-a-service.

avoid_when: Outside OpenStack environments.
name: OpenStack Barbican
raw: - [OpenStack Barbican](https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/Barbican) OSS - OpenStack secrets management. *Use when running OpenStack and need integrated key/secret management; avoid outside OpenStack environments.*
summary: OpenStack secrets management.
use_when: Running OpenStack and need integrated key/secret management.

avoid_when: You need machine-to-machine secret management (use Vault).
name: passbolt
raw: - [passbolt](https://www.passbolt.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Password manager for teams with self-hosted and paid offerings. *Use for team password sharing with GPG-based encryption and self-hosting; avoid if you need machine-to-machine secret management (use Vault).*
summary: Password manager for teams with self-hosted and paid offerings.
use_when: Team password sharing with GPG-based encryption and self-hosting.

avoid_when: You need dynamic secrets or centralized access control (use Vault).
name: SOPS
raw: - [SOPS](https://getsops.io/) OSS - Secrets management tool for GitOps/IaC (encrypt YAML/JSON/env). ([GitHub](https://github.com/getsops/sops)) *Use to encrypt secrets in Git alongside your IaC for GitOps workflows; avoid if you need dynamic secrets or centralized access control (use Vault).*
summary: Secrets management tool for GitOps/IaC (encrypt YAML/JSON/env).
use_when: Encrypt secrets in Git alongside your IaC for GitOps workflows.

avoid_when: You just need free public certs (use Let's Encrypt directly via cert-manager or Certbot).
name: Boulder (Let's Encrypt)
raw: - [Boulder (Let's Encrypt)](https://github.com/letsencrypt/boulder) OSS - ACME-based certificate authority server powering Let's Encrypt. *Use when you need to run your own ACME CA internally; avoid if you just need free public certs (use Let's Encrypt directly via cert-manager or Certbot).*
summary: ACME-based certificate authority server powering Let's Encrypt.
use_when: You need to run your own ACME CA internally.

avoid_when: You're on Kubernetes (use cert-manager instead).
name: CertMate
raw: - [CertMate](https://www.certmate.org/) OSS - Certificate management automation. ([GitHub](https://github.com/usual2970/certmate)) *Use for lightweight cert lifecycle automation; avoid if you're on Kubernetes (use cert-manager instead).*
summary: Certificate management automation.
use_when: Lightweight cert lifecycle automation.

avoid_when: For standard key management needs.
name: Cosmian KMS
raw: - [Cosmian KMS](https://cosmian.com/data-protection-suite/cosmian-kms/) - Key management service. *Use when you need privacy-enhancing cryptography (FHE, attribute-based encryption); avoid for standard key management needs.*
summary: Key management service.
use_when: You need privacy-enhancing cryptography (FHE, attribute-based encryption).

avoid_when: For cloud-native workloads where native KMS services suffice.
name: Entrust KeyControl
raw: - [Entrust KeyControl](https://www.entrust.com/products/key-management/keycontrol) - Key management for enterprise. *Use for enterprise KMIP-compliant key management with HSM integration; avoid for cloud-native workloads where native KMS services suffice.*
summary: Key management for enterprise.
use_when: Enterprise KMIP-compliant key management with HSM integration.

avoid_when: Cloud KMS or software-based solutions meet your compliance needs.
name: Futurex KMES Series 3
raw: - [Futurex KMES Series 3](https://www.futurex.com/products/key-management-server/kmes-series-3) - Hardware key management. *Use when you need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware key management; avoid if cloud KMS or software-based solutions meet your compliance needs.*
summary: Hardware key management.
use_when: You need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware key management.

avoid_when: You're not already invested in IBM infrastructure.
name: IBM Guardium Key Lifecycle Manager
raw: - [IBM Guardium Key Lifecycle Manager](https://www.ibm.com/products/guardium-key-lifecycle-manager) - Enterprise key management. *Use in IBM-centric environments needing encryption key lifecycle management; avoid if you're not already invested in IBM infrastructure.*
summary: Enterprise key management.
use_when: In IBM-centric environments needing encryption key lifecycle management.

avoid_when: For automated cert management in CI/CD.
name: Keystore Explorer
raw: - [Keystore Explorer](https://keystore-explorer.org/) OSS - GUI for managing keystores. ([GitHub](https://github.com/kaikramer/keystore-explorer)) *Use for visual inspection/editing of JKS/PKCS#12 keystores during development; avoid for automated cert management in CI/CD.*
summary: GUI for managing keystores.
use_when: Visual inspection/editing of JKS/PKCS#12 keystores during development.

avoid_when: For production or any non-local use case.
name: mkcert
raw: - [mkcert](https://github.com/FiloSottile/mkcert) OSS - Local SSL certificate generation. *Use for instant, trusted localhost TLS certs during development; avoid for production or any non-local use case.*
summary: Local SSL certificate generation.
use_when: Instant, trusted localhost TLS certs during development.

avoid_when: For simple TLS cert needs.
name: StrongKey
raw: - [StrongKey](https://www.strongkey.com/) - Enterprise key management. *Use for FIDO2/WebAuthn key management and compliance-driven PKI; avoid for simple TLS cert needs.*
summary: Enterprise key management.
use_when: FIDO2/WebAuthn key management and compliance-driven PKI.

avoid_when: A cloud-native KMS meets your requirements.
name: Thales CipherTrust Manager
raw: - [Thales CipherTrust Manager](https://cpl.thalesgroup.com/encryption/ciphertrust-manager) - Enterprise key and secret management. *Use for centralized encryption and key management across hybrid/multi-cloud with HSM backing; avoid if a cloud-native KMS meets your requirements.*
summary: Enterprise key and secret management.
use_when: Centralized encryption and key management across hybrid/multi-cloud with HSM backing.

avoid_when: For automated, large-scale PKI (use cert-manager, CFSSL, or step-ca).
name: XCA
raw: - [XCA](https://www.hohnstaedt.de/xca/) OSS - X.509 certificate and key management. *Use for managing a small internal CA with a desktop GUI; avoid for automated, large-scale PKI (use cert-manager, CFSSL, or step-ca).*
summary: X.509 certificate and key management.
use_when: Managing a small internal CA with a desktop GUI.

avoid_when: You need a full-featured IAM with user management (use Keycloak).
name: Dex
raw: - [Dex](https://dexidp.io/) OSS - OpenID Connect identity provider for Kubernetes and beyond. ([GitHub](https://github.com/dexidp/dex)) *Use as a lightweight OIDC federation layer to bridge upstream IdPs into K8s and GitOps tools; avoid if you need a full-featured IAM with user management (use Keycloak).*
summary: OpenID Connect identity provider for Kubernetes and beyond.
use_when: As a lightweight OIDC federation layer to bridge upstream IdPs into K8s and GitOps tools.

avoid_when: You only need IdP federation without user management (use Dex) or want a managed service.
name: Keycloak
raw: - [Keycloak](https://www.keycloak.org/) OSS - Open source identity and access management. ([GitHub](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak)) *Use for self-hosted SSO/OIDC/SAML with user federation and fine-grained authorization; avoid if you only need IdP federation without user management (use Dex) or want a managed service.*
summary: Open source identity and access management.
use_when: Self-hosted SSO/OIDC/SAML with user federation and fine-grained authorization.

avoid_when: You need a full PAM solution with session recording out of the box (use Teleport or JumpServer).
name: HashiCorp Boundary
raw: - [HashiCorp Boundary](https://boundaryproject.io/) Source-available - Secure remote access to systems. ([GitHub](https://github.com/hashicorp/boundary)) *Use for identity-based, zero-trust access to infrastructure without a traditional VPN; avoid if you need a full PAM solution with session recording out of the box (use Teleport or JumpServer).*
summary: Secure remote access to systems.
use_when: Identity-based, zero-trust access to infrastructure without a traditional VPN.

avoid_when: The project's maintenance status doesn't meet your support needs.
name: InfraHQ
raw: - [InfraHQ](https://infrahq.com/) OSS - Identity-aware access management / access proxy for infrastructure. ([GitHub](https://github.com/infrahq/infra)) *Use for SSO-based access to Kubernetes clusters and infrastructure; avoid if the project's maintenance status doesn't meet your support needs.*
summary: Identity-aware access management / access proxy for infrastructure.
use_when: SSO-based access to Kubernetes clusters and infrastructure.

avoid_when: You prefer agent-based zero-trust access (use Teleport/Boundary).
name: JumpServer
raw: - [JumpServer](https://www.jumpserver.com/) OSS - Open-source bastion host / privileged access management (PAM) platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver)) *Use for a self-hosted bastion with session recording, RBAC, and asset management; avoid if you prefer agent-based zero-trust access (use Teleport/Boundary).*
summary: Open-source bastion host / privileged access management (PAM) platform.
use_when: A self-hosted bastion with session recording, RBAC, and asset management.

avoid_when: You only need simple SSH bastion functionality (JumpServer is lighter).
name: Teleport
raw: - [Teleport](https://goteleport.com/) Open-core / SaaS - Secure access platform for SSH/Kubernetes/databases with OSS core and enterprise editions. ([GitHub](https://github.com/gravitational/teleport)) *Use for unified, certificate-based access to SSH/K8s/DB with audit logging; avoid if you only need simple SSH bastion functionality (JumpServer is lighter).*
summary: Secure access platform for SSH/Kubernetes/databases with OSS core and enterprise editions.
use_when: Unified, certificate-based access to SSH/K8s/DB with audit logging.

avoid_when: You're Kubernetes-only and want a lighter mesh (use Istio or Linkerd).
name: HashiCorp Consul
raw: - [HashiCorp Consul](https://www.consul.io/) Source-available - Service networking and discovery platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul)) *Use for service discovery and mesh across VMs and Kubernetes (multi-runtime); avoid if you're Kubernetes-only and want a lighter mesh (use Istio or Linkerd).*
summary: Service networking and discovery platform.
use_when: Service discovery and mesh across VMs and Kubernetes (multi-runtime).

avoid_when: For small clusters where the complexity and resource overhead aren't justified.
name: Istio
raw: - [Istio](https://istio.io/) OSS - Service mesh for managing microservices traffic. ([GitHub](https://github.com/istio/istio)) *Use when you need advanced traffic management, mTLS, and observability at scale; avoid for small clusters where the complexity and resource overhead aren't justified.*
summary: Service mesh for managing microservices traffic.
use_when: You need advanced traffic management, mTLS, and observability at scale.

avoid_when: You need advanced traffic routing, multi-cluster gateways, or Envoy ecosystem compatibility (use Istio).
name: Linkerd
raw: - [Linkerd](https://linkerd.io/) OSS - Lightweight service mesh for Kubernetes. ([GitHub](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2)) *Use when you want a minimal, Rust-based mesh with automatic mTLS and low operational overhead; avoid if you need advanced traffic routing, multi-cluster gateways, or Envoy ecosystem compatibility (use Istio).*
summary: Lightweight service mesh for Kubernetes.
use_when: You want a minimal, Rust-based mesh with automatic mTLS and low operational overhead.

avoid_when: Teams are small and agile—overhead can slow you down.
name: Jira
raw: - [Jira](https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira) - Issue tracking and project management platform by Atlassian. *Use when you need deep workflow customization and enterprise integrations; avoid when teams are small and agile—overhead can slow you down.*
summary: Issue tracking and project management platform by Atlassian.
use_when: You need deep workflow customization and enterprise integrations.

avoid_when: You need a mature plugin ecosystem or enterprise support today.
name: Plane
raw: - [Plane](https://plane.so/) OSS - Open-source project management tool. ([GitHub](https://github.com/makeplane/plane)) *Use when you want a self-hosted, lightweight Jira alternative; avoid when you need a mature plugin ecosystem or enterprise support today.*
summary: Open-source project management tool.
use_when: You want a self-hosted, lightweight Jira alternative.

avoid_when: You want developer-friendly scripting—its XML-based test plans age poorly in version control.
name: Apache JMeter
raw: - [Apache JMeter](https://jmeter.apache.org/) OSS - Load testing and performance measurement tool. ([GitHub](https://github.com/apache/jmeter)) *Use when you need protocol-level load testing (HTTP, JDBC, JMS, etc.); avoid when you want developer-friendly scripting—its XML-based test plans age poorly in version control.*
summary: Load testing and performance measurement tool.
use_when: You need protocol-level load testing (HTTP, JDBC, JMS, etc.).

avoid_when: You need advanced protocol support beyond HTTP/WebSocket/Socket.io.
name: Artillery
raw: - [Artillery](https://www.artillery.io/) OSS - Modern load testing toolkit. ([GitHub](https://github.com/artilleryio/artillery)) *Use when you want YAML-driven load tests that fit naturally in CI pipelines; avoid when you need advanced protocol support beyond HTTP/WebSocket/Socket.io.*
summary: Modern load testing toolkit.
use_when: You want YAML-driven load tests that fit naturally in CI pipelines.

avoid_when: You need multi-tab, multi-origin, or non-Chromium browser coverage (consider Playwright instead).
name: Cypress
raw: - [Cypress](https://www.cypress.io/) Open-core / SaaS - End-to-end testing for web applications. ([GitHub](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress)) *Use when you test single-origin SPAs and want great DX with time-travel debugging; avoid when you need multi-tab, multi-origin, or non-Chromium browser coverage (consider Playwright instead).*
summary: End-to-end testing for web applications.
use_when: You test single-origin SPAs and want great DX with time-travel debugging.

avoid_when: Your team prefers code-first testing or the wiki paradigm feels outdated.
name: FitNesse
raw: - [FitNesse](https://fitnesse.org/) OSS - Acceptance testing framework. ([GitHub](https://github.com/unclebob/fitnesse)) *Use when business stakeholders write acceptance criteria in wiki-style tables; avoid when your team prefers code-first testing or the wiki paradigm feels outdated.*
summary: Acceptance testing framework.
use_when: Business stakeholders write acceptance criteria in wiki-style tables.

avoid_when: You need a GUI-based test builder or non-HTTP protocol support without extensions.
name: k6
raw: - [k6](https://k6.io/) OSS - Load testing tool for performance testing. ([GitHub](https://github.com/grafana/k6)) *Use when developers want to write load tests in JavaScript with a CLI-first workflow; avoid when you need a GUI-based test builder or non-HTTP protocol support without extensions.*
summary: Load testing tool for performance testing.
use_when: Developers want to write load tests in JavaScript with a CLI-first workflow.

avoid_when: You want full OSS freedom or fine-grained CI scripting control.
name: Katalon Studio
raw: - [Katalon Studio](https://katalon.com/) - Automated testing for web, API, and mobile. ([GitHub](https://github.com/katalon-studio)) *Use when QA teams need a low-code, all-in-one testing IDE; avoid when you want full OSS freedom or fine-grained CI scripting control.*
summary: Automated testing for web, API, and mobile.
use_when: QA teams need a low-code, all-in-one testing IDE.

raw: - [Grafana MCP](https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana) OSS - Model Context Protocol for Grafana. - **Use when** you want AI assistants to query dashboards, alerts, and data sources in Grafana. **Avoid when** you don't use Grafana or prefer direct API integrations over MCP.
summary: Model Context Protocol for Grafana.
use_when: You want AI assistants to query dashboards, alerts, and data sources in Grafana.

avoid_when: Security policy forbids AI-agent access to your clusters or you don't run Kubernetes.
name: mcp-server-kubernetes
raw: - [mcp-server-kubernetes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-server-kubernetes) OSS - Node MCP server for interacting with Kubernetes clusters via kubectl. ([GitHub](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers)) - **Use when** you want AI tools to inspect and manage Kubernetes resources through MCP. **Avoid when** security policy forbids AI-agent access to your clusters or you don't run Kubernetes.
summary: Node MCP server for interacting with Kubernetes clusters via kubectl.
use_when: You want AI tools to inspect and manage Kubernetes resources through MCP.

avoid_when: You have a single-agent use case or prefer mature frameworks like LangGraph or CrewAI.
name: genai-agentos
raw: - [genai-agentos](https://github.com/genai-works-org/genai-agentos) OSS - Framework for building, running, and managing multi-agent AI workflows. - **Use when** you're building multi-agent systems and need a lightweight orchestration framework. **Avoid when** you have a single-agent use case or prefer mature frameworks like LangGraph or CrewAI.
summary: Framework for building, running, and managing multi-agent AI workflows.
use_when: You're building multi-agent systems and need a lightweight orchestration framework.

avoid_when: You're not running LLM workloads or already have sufficient observability through your existing stack.
name: Arize Phoenix
raw: - [Arize Phoenix](https://arize.com/docs/phoenix) OSS - LLM observability and evaluation platform. ([GitHub](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix)) - **Use when** you need tracing, evaluation, and debugging for LLM applications with a self-hosted option. **Avoid when** you're not running LLM workloads or already have sufficient observability through your existing stack.
summary: LLM observability and evaluation platform.
use_when: You need tracing, evaluation, and debugging for LLM applications with a self-hosted option.

avoid_when: You have minimal LLM usage and don't need per-request cost/latency tracking.
name: Langfuse
raw: - [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) Open-core / SaaS - LLM observability and analytics; OSS self-hosted core with commercial cloud offering. ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) - **Use when** you want detailed LLM trace analytics with the option to self-host or use managed cloud. **Avoid when** you have minimal LLM usage and don't need per-request cost/latency tracking.
summary: LLM observability and analytics; OSS self-hosted core with commercial cloud offering.
use_when: You want detailed LLM trace analytics with the option to self-host or use managed cloud.

name: LangSmith
raw: - [LangSmith](https://smith.langchain.com/) Open-core / SaaS - LLM application development platform with observability, testing, and evaluation (LangChain-affiliated). - **Use when** you're already using LangChain and want tightly integrated tracing, testing, and prompt management. **Avoid when** you don't use LangChain—vendor lock-in to the LangChain ecosystem may not be worth it.
summary: LLM application development platform with observability, testing, and evaluation (LangChain-affiliated).
use_when: You're already using LangChain and want tightly integrated tracing, testing, and prompt management.
